summary: A 1964 steel tower on Kendrick Peak replaced a 1930s L-4 cab and a 1911 lookout cabin; sources disagree on whether it is still active.

facts.design: 10 ft steel tower with 14x14 ft flat-roof cab and catwalk (1964); earlier L-4 cab (early 1930s) and 1911 log cabin lookout
facts.status_note: NHLR (updated 2016) describes it as in active service; Wikipedia separately reports the Forest Service describes it as open to visitors when staffed in summer, but also says it appeared damaged and likely abandoned as of 2024, uncited. The Forest Service's own trail page does not mention staffing at all. Not resolved.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Kaibab National Forest, Williams Ranger District

visit.trail_note: Reached via Kendrick Mountain Trail #22, about 27 miles from Williams, AZ

events.note: Log cabin built about a quarter mile below the summit as sleeping quarters; first used as a fire lookout in 1912 (NHLR calls it the second-oldest fire-detection structure in AZ/NM)
L-4 cab erected on the peak (early 1930s, exact year not given)
Current 10 ft steel tower with 14x14 ft flat-roof cab replaced the L-4 structure
Cabin listed on National Register of Historic Places as 'Kendrick Lookout Tower and Cabin', January 28, 1988
Registered February 21, 1994 as NHLR US 78, AZ 1
Cabin wrapped in protective material during the Pumpkin Fire; structures survived
Cabin wrapped in protective material again during the Boundary Fire; structures survived

sources.title: Kendrick Mountain Trail #22
sources.publisher: Kaibab National Forest, U.S. Forest Service

photos.credit: Dyan Bone / U.S. Forest Service, Southwestern Region, Kaibab National Forest
photos.caption: The lookout tower seen from below, 2016

notes_for_editor: Current operational status is genuinely disputed between sources: NHLR (page last updated 2016) describes the tower as in active service, and Wikipedia separately attributes a 'open to visitors when staffed in summer' description to the Forest Service -- but checked directly, the USFS Kendrick Mountain Trail #22 page itself says nothing about staffing or visitor access, so that claim should not be cited to the trail page. Wikipedia also says the tower looked damaged and likely abandoned as of mid-2024, with no cited source for that claim. Worth a human check (e.g. a recent trip report or current USFS fire lookout roster) before updating the tower's staffing/access fields. The tower record's 'kind' field (two_story) comes from FFLA's '2-Story Cab' classification, which doesn't obviously match NHLR's description of a flat-roof cab on a 10 ft tower -- plausibly just differing naming conventions rather than a real conflict, so no correction proposed, but flagging it.
